Its 'Test' line joins testHelpers with link-cli spend-request as an undifferentiated OR, whereas the May raw labels the helper test simulation at lines 23-25 and the Link CLI flow 'Test your live mode integration' at lines 52-77, including --request-approval. Flag the concept's unqualified present-tense eligibility claim at wiki/concepts/stripe-shared-payment-tokens.md:10 ('US only') and, if retained as current support, its payment-method list at line 56. The May raw states US availability at line 8 and method conditions at lines 329-340; the November index at lines 5-15 establishes neither current geography nor supported methods. A query about current US-only eligibility or current Affirm support could receive a falsely current answer. Recommend dating these as May-capture claims and preserving Affirm's buyer-controlled UI limitation, without inferring changed eligibility.

Flag wiki/concepts/stripe-shared-payment-tokens.md:64, which equates the issued-token 'used' webhook with 'Seller charged the SPT'. The May raw line 430 defines 'used' as the seller using the SPT; lines 82-100 describe creating and confirming a PaymentIntent, and lines 428-431 distinguish token states without proving a succeeded payment. A query 'Does used mean my payment succeeded?' would get a misleading finality answer. Recommend 'seller used the SPT' and keep payment outcome separate from token state.
